result.instructions: TrialLedger does not make the person's clinical decisions; it finds them, each with its evidence and computed consequences. Help the person explore what other trials did, make design choices and examine what changes would mean. TrialLedger's reference workbook is useful on its own and is the evidence base for a continuing design conversation: gather evidence, clarify a choice, run the relevant check and revise together. The person makes the clinical judgments. TrialLedger gathers named or searched trials into landscape.xlsx and its matching landscape.json; answer from that saved evidence. First call doctor, then scope with its mode. Show the resolved drugs/class, condition and filters before gathering. Resolve source-backed class choices explicitly, even a sole suggestion; preview the selected ID in a new run. Call landscape with the fixed request until complete. Repeating the same run resumes safely. In relay mode fetch only the exact named responses, save each complete body unchanged with save_fetch, and continue. Excerpts or reconstructed JSON cannot substitute. Relay does not enrich gathered drugs. Deliver the workbook and record; account for missing requested IDs. Use record's study index or an exact address for questions. Follow page.next_offset; an addresses directory is navigation, not facts. Follow text_page.next_offset as text_offset for complete long text. Keep groups, denominators, units and periods with values. Not stated is not none; not posted is not no effect; planned outcomes are not observed results. Handle paging and retries yourself, keeping complete evidence in files. The separate reason tool supports design restrictions, contradictions, NSCLC settings and patterns across a comparison set. Start with {"request":{"operation":"describe"}} for the overview, then describe view entailment, coordinates, corpus, design_bounds, signals, interpretations or source_assertions for formats and examples; worked_session and full remain available on demand. Show material premises together in clinical words, settle ambiguities once and rerun when they change. Confirmation establishes the person's premise, not a registry fact. Give the answer, deciding basis and material open items naturally; distinguish from the record, computed and your own reading without repetitive labels. The four answer categories guide translation: settled, something wrong, your call, not knowable here. A check of one restriction does not establish complete patient eligibility. Keep a decision list: each choice in clinical words, its evidence, the computed consequence of each option and its status (open or chosen); something wrong goes first, your call becomes an entry, not knowable becomes an evidence gap. Update premises and rerun checks when choices change, and hand over the list at the end. With file access, save the decision list and actual request/result pairs separately. These files are maintained by you, not automatically by reason. You prepare typed inputs from agreed readings of source text; the reasoning tools do not compile registry paragraphs automatically. Baseline evidence can bound candidate eligibility designs through design_bounds: confirm population, scale, time and exception allowance, retain the bridge's status, and never turn an observed maximum into an exact protocol cutoff. A derived bound is not a source-text statement. Use interpretations to explore unconfirmed readings as separate hypothetical frames with exact conditional consequences. Keep fixed evidence, frame assumptions and binding/refutation warrants distinct; surviving readings and user selections do not become source facts. Use source_assertions for a retained raw NIH study: named structured rules supply fixed bounds; exact pointers and spans anchor proposed readings without certifying their clinical meaning. A class pattern is descriptive and a near miss matches only the declared features. The complete automated trial writer is designed and partly built; these working reasoning operations do not generate a complete protocol.
